categories.main_business_segments: MGM Resorts International operates through three main business segments: Las Vegas Strip Resorts, Regional Operations, and MGM China. Las Vegas Strip Resorts includes major properties such as Bellagio, MGM Grand Las Vegas, Mandalay Bay, and others on the Las Vegas Strip. Regional Operations covers casino resorts in various U.S. states outside Nevada, such as MGM Grand Detroit and Borgata in Atlantic City. MGM China operates integrated casino resorts in Macau, including MGM Macau and MGM Cotai.
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: The company’s core operations are based on integrated resort management, combining casino gaming, hotel accommodations, entertainment, dining, and retail. MGM leverages advanced data analytics, digital platforms, and loyalty programs to enhance customer experience and operational efficiency. In addition, MGM invests in digital gaming technologies through BetMGM for online sports betting and iGaming, and utilizes state-of-the-art facilities and amenities to differentiate its properties.
categories.primary_customers_markets: MGM serves a diverse customer base including premium gaming customers, leisure travelers, business and convention guests, and regional gaming patrons. In Macau, the focus is on main floor gaming customers and mass market segments, with a declining emphasis on VIP gaming. The company targets both domestic and international tourists, business travelers, and local/regional gaming markets.
categories.geographic_coverage: MGM operates primarily in the United States, with a concentration on the Las Vegas Strip and additional properties in Michigan, Mississippi, New Jersey, Maryland, Massachusetts, Ohio, and New York. Internationally, MGM China operates in Macau, and the company is pursuing development opportunities in Japan. The company’s reach extends to both North American and Asian gaming and hospitality markets.
categories.supply_chain_position: MGM operates at the downstream end of the hospitality and gaming supply chain, directly serving end customers through its owned and managed resorts. The company is primarily a service provider, integrating real estate, gaming, hotel, entertainment, and food and beverage offerings. MGM has shifted to an asset-light model, leasing most of its real estate assets while focusing on operations and customer experience.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: MGM’s strategic focus is on becoming the world’s premier gaming entertainment company through an asset-light model, digital transformation, and international expansion. Key initiatives include investment in online sports betting and iGaming via BetMGM, development of an integrated resort in Japan, operational excellence, and customer-centric innovation. The company also emphasizes ESG (environmental, social, and governance) leadership, diversity and inclusion, and disciplined capital allocation.
categories.revenue_model: MGM generates revenue primarily from casino gaming, hotel room sales, food and beverage, entertainment, and retail operations. Additional revenue streams include online sports betting and iGaming (BetMGM), management fees, and lease income from third-party operators. The majority of Las Vegas Strip revenue is from non-gaming sources, while regional and Macau operations are more gaming-centric.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: MGM competes with other major integrated resort and gaming companies such as Caesars Entertainment, Wynn Resorts, Las Vegas Sands, and regional/local casino operators. In Macau, competition includes five other concessionaires and subconcessionaires. MGM positions itself as a leader in high-quality, integrated resort experiences, with a strong brand and diversified offerings across gaming and non-gaming segments.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: For the year ended December 31, 2021, MGM reported net revenues of $9.7 billion, rebounding from $5.2 billion in 2020 but below pre-pandemic levels of $12.9 billion in 2019. The company has a large asset base, significant cash reserves, and a substantial debt load ($12.9 billion principal as of year-end 2021). MGM has demonstrated strong recovery post-pandemic, with growth driven by the return of travel, strategic acquisitions, and digital expansion.
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: MGM’s value proposition centers on delivering extraordinary, integrated entertainment experiences through premier resorts, superior amenities, and personalized service. The company differentiates itself with iconic brands, a broad portfolio of properties, advanced loyalty programs, and a growing digital presence. MGM emphasizes quality, innovation, and customer-centricity, aiming to provide unique, memorable experiences that drive loyalty and repeat visitation.
